chunks: Ibn Abi Jayyad informed us from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim al-Barqi from Muhammad ibn Ali Abu Samina al-Kufi from Hammad ibn Isa from Ibrahim ibn Umar from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilali from Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari from Abdullah ibn Abbas, who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said in his will to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him): O Ali, indeed Quraish will overpower you and their unity will gather against your oppression and subjugation. So if you find helpers, strive against them in Jihad, and if you do not find helpers, restrain your hand and preserve your blood, for martyrdom is behind you. May Allah curse the one who kills you.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali
key_terms.جِهَادٌ: Striving or fighting in the path of God
key_terms.قُرَيْشٌ: Quraish, the prominent tribe of Mecca

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say to Imam Ali in his will regarding Quraish and his martyrdom?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the political tension between the Prophet’s family and the Quraysh, framing Imam Ali’s eventual martyrdom not merely as a battle outcome but as a divinely ordained destiny following a period of strategic patience. The hadith underscores the Shia concept of *ghayba* (occultation) and leadership continuity by linking Ali’s restraint to the preservation of the Imamate, a theme central to the chapter’s discussion on the Mahdi’s lineage from Imam Husain.
